source.version: Author manuscript nihms-2151735.pdf; available in PMC 2026 March 13; final-edited citation October 2024

enumeration.method: Independent bold-heading enumeration and visual comparison of both complete Theorems.

checks: Both original main-text Theorems are complete, each with its two distinct parts. Theorem 1 has null and local-alternative normal limits; Theorem 2 has lower and upper detection bounds. All main-text theorem headings through page 23 were independently enumerated.

Fourteen original entries and ten auxiliary passages preserve the iid linear model, hypotheses, both score versions, W_n, the sample covariance, separate squared-covariance estimator, studentized statistic, A1-A2, local alternative, REM, rejection rule and prior-average risk. Unnamed population normalization and source conventions remain available as auxiliary passages.

Independent reconstruction confirms 13 direct uses and 23 related connections. Theorem 1 uses both sample-based T_n and the population covariance in its shift. Theorem 2 does not acquire the deterministic local alternative or population-score interface, and Theorem 1 does not acquire the REM or all-tests risk.

Gaussian errors belong only to Theorem 2(i). Its part (ii) does not explicitly print k_n=o(sqrt(p)); the proof-only reference to Theorem 1 is recorded without importing that condition. A1 factorizes coordinate moments only through total degree four; full coordinate independence is not inserted.

Visual review distinguishes the hat on Sigma_Z squared from the square of Sigma-hat_Z, checks both lines of (6), retains matrix squares and off-diagonal pairs, and distinguishes the population trace in (8) from the estimated denominator in (5). The page-11 population comparison notation is z^0, with superscript zero.

Ten source conventions or ambiguities are retained, including population covariance aliasing, score reuse, normalization domains, finite/asymptotic variance notation, nonsingularity for the score equivalence, REM support/tail conventions and the asymptotic testing criterion. No appendix content or unquoted correction is added.

Every entry uses literal source terms and faithful definition/assumption/source-passage headings. Symbol and assumption-label selectors are checked against the original passage or related Theorem, and every connection has a source-specific explanation.

All six JSON content artifacts reproduce byte for byte from the retained per-paper scripts. Frozen hashes and independent source-specific checks protect the reviewed state; rerunning scripts alone is not a new semantic audit or proof certification.

source_notes.description: The source deliberately reuses z_i for population-centered and sample-centered scores. The latter share estimated means. Separate original entries and the explicit page-11 convention retain this distinction.

The Omega display uses Sigma_Z without a separate displayed Sigma_Z:=Cov(z) definition. The adjacent variance expression and population-score derivation identify the intended population covariance. This correspondence is recorded as interpretation supported by those passages.
Equation (6) defines an estimate of Sigma_Z squared with off-diagonal matrix products. It is not (Sigma-hat_Z)^2. Both lines, the hat placement and matrix-square operations are retained.

The source does not prescribe a fallback if the estimated trace in T_n is zero or negative, or separately state positivity of every population denominator. No truncation, absolute value or replacement estimator is added.

Pages 4 and 9 write Var(W_n)=sigma_n^2 with a 2/n^2 formula, while page 9 also gives a preceding asymptotic variance expansion. The census preserves the displayed normalization without silently changing n^2 to n(n-1).

The coefficient-to-score null equivalence on page 3 assumes nonsingular Sigma_X. Theorem preambles print an upper bound on its largest eigenvalue, without an explicit lower spectral bound. The equivalence condition is preserved separately rather than inserted into all results.

Theorem 2(ii) prints the directional k_n quadratic-form condition, but not Theorem 1 k_n=o(sqrt(p)). Its proof refers to Theorem 1 for null calibration. Preserve this mismatch in stated scope; do not silently inherit the omitted condition or the local alternative.

REM specifies S=p^(1-s), uniform size-S support and nonzero iid sub-Gaussian coefficients with variance gamma^2. It gives no rounding rule for noninteger S and no explicit uniform sub-Gaussian proxy constant in the inspected definition. The variance is not relabeled as a proxy.

REM is written for beta itself, while the general null is beta=beta_0. Theorem 2 proof sets beta_0=0 and sigma^2=1 without loss of generality. This normalization is retained as source context, without rewriting the REM as a quoted prior on beta-beta_0.

Theorem 2 uses powerful/powerless without a separate formal definition of the asymptotic error limits in its preamble. The main text supplies the prior-average risk on page 13 and the proposed statistic divergence criterion on page 17. A fixed-size normal-quantile test is not silently replaced by a vanishing-size rule, and likelihood-ratio proof machinery is not treated as a required API.

ambient_resolution.T1: The iid linear model and coefficient null are D1-D2. The proposed statistic is D8, using sample scores D4, W_n D5 and estimators D6-D7. A1-A2 are D9-D10. Part (ii) uses local alternative D11; delta_z is defined in the statement. Omega is original local formula A1 with population score covariance D3. Alpha,k_n and spectral/rate conditions are locally stated; n,p are asymptotic model dimensions. Part (i) does not assume Ha.
ambient_resolution.T2: The model D1, assumptions D9-D10 and REM D12 are common. Gamma_0 squared is defined inside the theorem. The lower bound (i) additionally assumes Gaussian errors and concerns all binary tests, with source average-risk convention D14. The upper bound (ii) concerns the proposed rejection rule D13, hence T_n and its sample estimators; it does not acquire the population local alternative D11 or Theorem 1 k_n=o(sqrt(p)) by implication. Sub-Gaussian coefficients are part of the REM, not an error-law assumption.

source_claim_references.to_source_label: Assumptions A1 and A2; local alternative (7)
source_claim_references.scope: A1-A2 in both parts; the deterministic local alternative only in part (ii).
A1-A2 and REM with s in [0,1/2] in both parts. Additional Gaussian errors only in (i); tuning-vector restrictions only in (ii).
Page-17 proof invokes the null calibration result. No theorem-to-theorem statement edge and no automatic inheritance of Theorem 1 assumptions.

review_limits: Registered NIH author manuscript identified by filename and hash; no claim of byte-equivalence to the final typeset journal article.
Original source conventions and ambiguities are retained separately; no appendix material is used in the census.
Source and schema validation do not certify mathematical proofs.
